name: Sprocket
text: Run the canary rollout at 5% traffic for the new prompt engine. It’s the fastest way to catch silent failures without risking user impact. The trade-off is delayed full deployment, but that’s better than a rollback under load.

name: Gauge
text: Canary at 5% still misses the real risk: silent failures only show up when users hit them, not when traffic is low. A better alternative is a shadow test that replays real user traffic against the new engine in parallel, comparing outputs before any traffic shift. Settle it with a controlled A/B where shadow results match production behavior within a tight tolerance—if they don’t, no rollout until the gap closes.

name: Sprocket
text:
Run a shadow test first: replay 100% of real user traffic through the new prompt engine in parallel, compare outputs to the old engine, and log mismatches. This catches silent failures before any user sees them, at the cost of doubling compute load during the test. Only after we’re confident in the outputs do we shift 5% traffic to the new engine for the canary.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow testing replays traffic but misses the real risk: it only catches mismatches in *output*, not in *behavior*—like when the new engine silently corrupts data or triggers downstream failures the old one never did. A better alternative is a staged rollout with synthetic canaries: inject controlled, high-risk inputs (edge cases, adversarial prompts) into the new engine at 0% traffic, measure stability and side effects, then expand only if those pass. Settle it by running both: shadow test to catch output drift, synthetic canaries to stress-test behavior, and only then shift real traffic.
